narrative.text: The README's opening banner image for the GITB Interoperability Test Bed; it carries no text of its own.

Introduces the Interoperability Test Bed, a European Commission DIGIT service for conformance testing of IT systems through scenario-based test cases written in the GITB Test Description Language (TDL), whose steps use built-in capabilities or orchestrate extension services. Test cases typically exchange and validate messages with a system under test, and may include control flow, user interaction and data processing; the Test Bed also offers a user interface, a REST API and webhooks. DIGIT runs a shared instance and publishes all components as Docker images for local use. The section opens with build, quality, licence, documentation and Docker badges.

Says the repository holds the Test Bed's two main application components: the test engine, which executes test cases and reports progress and outcome (Docker image gitb-srv), and the frontend, which provides the user interface and test, user and configuration management (gitb-ui). It notes that the simplest way to use the Test Bed is through the published Docker images and the installation guide, with building from source as the alternative.

Points to the Test Bed's documentation hub on the Interoperable Europe Portal and lists highlights: the developer onboarding guide, the user guide, reference documentation for GITB TDL and GITB test services, and installation guides for development and production. Newcomers are advised to start with the onboarding guide and then follow tutorials on a first test case, simple messaging and complex testing.

States that gitb-srv and gitb-ui are both Java-based: gitb-srv is a Spring Boot application using Akka internally, gitb-ui is written in Scala on the Play Framework, and gitb-ui's frontend is an Angular TypeScript app built with Angular CLI.

Notes that the main configuration file is gitb-ui's application.conf, which never needs direct editing because every property can be set through environment variables, via Docker or the IDE; the full list of properties is documented in the production installation guide.
Heading that introduces the steps to build and run the components for development; it carries no further content.

Lists the tools needed to build and run the components: JDK 21+, Maven 3.9+ (for gitb-srv), SBT 1.10+ and Scala 2.13+ (for gitb-ui's backend) and Node 22+ (for gitb-ui's frontend), with IntelliJ and VS Code suggested but not required.

Notes that a complete Test Bed instance also needs a MySQL 8+ database for persistence and a Redis 7+ instance for session caching, both set up separately, and gives docker run commands for the isaitb/gitb-mysql and isaitb/gitb-redis images; all images are defined in docker-compose.yml.

Gives the development steps for gitb-srv: build with mvn clean install -DskipTests=true, run it either as a Java application with entry class Application in the gitb-testbed-service module (preferred, for direct debugging) or with mvn spring-boot:run, and set the environment variables remote.testcase.repository.url and remote.testresource.repository.url to the local gitb-ui repository endpoints on port 9000.

Gives the development steps for gitb-ui: sbt compile, a run configuration for sbt run, and environment variables as needed (e.g. THEME = ec), then npm install in gitb-ui/ui before choosing one of two ways to work on the Angular app. When developing with EU Login, SESSION_SECURE must be false and SESSION_COOKIE_NAME ITB_SESSION, or session cookies are never served over HTTP and authentication loops; testing over HTTPS through a local SSL proxy is the alternative.

Describes the first way to develop the Angular UI: build it with npm run build (or npm run build:dev to rebuild on change) into the Play application's assets and reach it through the Play welcome page at localhost:9000, refreshing the browser after rebuilds. This mirrors production and is needed to test interactions with the Play application, such as EU Login and the various login options.

Describes the second way to develop the Angular UI: run npm run build once for static resources, then npm start to serve the app at localhost:4200 with automatic reload, using the Play application only through its proxied REST API. It is the most efficient approach but cannot test Play interactions such as EU Login, although it can be used after authenticating through Play since cookies are shared.
Heading that introduces building the components as a Dockerised service, by one of two approaches: with the project's development tools, or with Docker Compose as a containerised build.

Says building with the development tools suits a repository already set up for development: it is faster but requires Java, Maven, NPM, SBT and Scala to be installed and the Docker images to be built by hand.

Gives the deployment build steps for gitb-srv: run mvn clean install -DskipTests=true -Denv=docker from the root, copy gitb-testbed-service/target/itbsrv.war to a separate folder, and build the isaitb/gitb-srv image there with the Dockerfile from etc/docker/gitb-srv.

Gives the deployment build steps for gitb-ui: run sbt clean dist (which also runs the Angular production build), unzip gitb-ui/target/universal/gitb-1.0-SNAPSHOT.zip into a folder named gitb-ui, and build the isaitb/gitb-ui image there with the Dockerfile from etc/docker/gitb-ui.
Gives the one step to build the database image: docker build -t isaitb/gitb-mysql from the etc/docker/gitb-mysql folder.
Gives the one step to build the session-cache image: docker build -t isaitb/gitb-redis from the etc/docker/gitb-redis folder.

Explains how to assemble the service from locally built images: follow the development installation guide, create or download a docker-compose.yml that uses those images, and start it with docker compose up -d.

Describes the containerised build with Docker Compose 2.0.0 or later, which builds all images from source with no developer tools but is slower. Six variables must be set first, and some are embedded in the images as build arguments: MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD, MYSQL_PASSWORD, DB_DEFAULT_PASSWORD (which must match MYSQL_PASSWORD), APPLICATION_SECRET, MASTER_PASSWORD and HMAC_KEY (shared by gitb-ui and gitb-srv). It gives example settings for Linux/macOS and PowerShell or a .env file, then docker compose up -d --build. These images are for development, and the published images still support runtime secrets via environment variables and _FILE variants.

Explains first access to a running Test Bed: go to localhost:9000, click login and authenticate as admin@itb with a one-time password, refreshed at each start-up until the first login, that is printed in the gitb-ui container logs (an example log excerpt is shown). The user guide and sample tutorials cover what comes next.
States that the software is released under the European Union Public Licence (EUPL) 1.2, with third-party licences and notices listed in NOTICE.md.

Says the authors waive all liability for the software's use or the interpretation of its results, that any data it stores, private data included, depends on the downstream user's configuration, and that the European Commission's shared instance has its own legal notice on its welcome page.
Invites feedback and questions about the GITB Test Bed software as issues in the repository, or by email to the Test Bed team at DIGIT-ITB@ec.europa.eu.

Refers readers to the Interoperable Europe Portal site for general information on the Test Bed and GITB, and, for standalone data validation rather than a full conformance testing platform, to the Test Bed's separate XML, RDF (SHACL), JSON and CSV validators.
